title: The Hypertext Transfer Protocol Status Code 308 (Permanent Redirect)
summary: Adds HTTP status code 308, Permanent Redirect. It works like 301 but requires the client to repeat the request with the same method and body, so a POST stays a POST. It was replaced by RFC 9110.

eli5.summary: A sign that says this shop has moved forever, and please bring your order to the new address exactly as you wrote it.

subtitle: A permanent redirect that keeps the request method unchanged.

tldr.problem: HTTP status 301 (Moved Permanently) and 302 (Found) allow clients to change a POST request to GET on redirect, but sometimes servers need to ensure the method stays the same.
tldr.mechanism: Status code 308 (Permanent Redirect) works like 301 but requires the client to repeat the request with the same method and message body, so POST stays POST and PUT stays PUT.
tldr.outcome: 308 filled a gap in HTTP semantics and was incorporated into RFC 9110, the consolidated HTTP specification.

today: RFC 7538 standardized HTTP status code 308 (Permanent Redirect). The specification is now incorporated in RFC 9110, the consolidated HTTP specification, as part of the modern HTTP standard.

sections.title: Permanent Redirect Status Code
sections.content:
HTTP redirects tell clients that a resource has moved to a new location, using a Location header field to specify the new URI. The status code tells the client whether the move is temporary or permanent and whether the request method can change.

Status code 301 (Moved Permanently) and 302 (Found) are permanent and temporary redirects, respectively, but both allow the client to change the request method from POST to GET. Status code 307 (Temporary Redirect) is the temporary variant that does NOT allow method change.

This RFC defines status code 308, filling the missing permanent redirect that does NOT allow method change. It works exactly like 307 but signals permanence instead of temporariness. A POST request redirected with 308 must be resubmitted as a POST to the new URI, preserving the request body and semantics.
sections.eli5: When redirecting a request, the server can say: this is temporary (307) or permanent (308), and the client must repeat the exact same request.

sections.title: How 308 Differs from 301
sections.content:
Status code 301 (Moved Permanently) is a permanent redirect but historically allows the user agent to convert the request method from POST to GET and discard the message body. Most web browsers do this, making 301 unsuitable when a server requires the same method to be used at the new URI.

Status code 308 (Permanent Redirect) indicates that the target resource has been permanently assigned a new URI and future references should use the new URI. Like 307 (Temporary Redirect), it does not allow changing the request method. A user agent receiving 308 MUST use the same request method and body when accessing the new URI. The response is cacheable by default unless the method definition or explicit cache control directives indicate otherwise.

Servers SHOULD include a Location header field containing the new URI, and MAY include a response body with a hyperlink to the new location. Clients MAY use the Location field for automatic redirection.
sections.eli5: A POST request that gets 301 might become a GET (wrong). A POST request that gets 308 stays a POST (correct).

sections.title: Deployment Considerations
sections.content:
HTTP specifies that recipients of unknown 3xx status codes should treat them the same as 300 (Multiple Choices). This means servers cannot rely on automatic 308 handling by all clients, especially older implementations. Therefore, servers should only use 308 when they have good confidence that clients understand the code or when fallback to 300 semantics is acceptable.

Server implementers are advised against User-Agent sniffing (varying the status code based on the User-Agent header), as this approach is difficult to maintain and debug, and requires special cache handling. HTML-based user agents can provide a fallback by sending an HTML response with a <meta http-equiv="refresh"> directive that users can click on.
sections.eli5: Older browsers might not understand 308, so servers should only use it when clients are known to support it, or when showing a link manually is acceptable.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
Status code 308 inherits the security considerations that apply to all HTTP redirects. If communication is not secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS), an attacker on the network can modify redirect status codes or target URIs to redirect requests to malicious servers. This could cause clients to send requests (including data in POST bodies) to unintended destinations.

Using HTTPS (HTTP over TLS) protects against these attacks by ensuring the integrity and authenticity of the status code and the Location header field.
sections.eli5: Without encryption, an attacker on the network could change where a browser is being redirected, potentially stealing data. Using HTTPS protects against this.
